title: Power Display flyout doesn't respect playback status of some monitors
summary: Power Display reportedly shows a volume control for a monitor whose playback endpoint was disabled in Windows Sound settings.

judgment.rationale: The endpoint-state transition is clear, but Windows endpoint enumeration versus flyout cache is unknown. Reproduce disable/reopen before selecting which layer to fix.
evidence: Reporter disables monitor playback device in Windows Sound settings and still sees a Power Display volume control.
Current Power Display has monitor view-model and end-to-end test areas.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce disable/re-enable and trace control state.

fix_assessment.rationale: Applicable if disabled endpoint remains exposed; reproduce before choosing enumeration versus refresh fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Hide Power Display control for disabled playback endpoints
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Power Display uses stale or incomplete playback-endpoint state when deciding control visibility.
plan: Reproduce enabled then disabled endpoint transition.
Trace view-model state/refresh; fix confirmed condition and add endpoint-state regression.
verification: Disabled endpoint has no active control after flyout reopen; re-enabling restores it.

confidence.rationale: Direct state mismatch and relevant view model, but enumeration versus refresh unknown.

reproduce.title: Hide Power Display control for disabled playback endpoints
prerequisites: Monitor playback endpoint and Power Display enabled
steps: 1. Open flyout and note volume control.
2. Disable endpoint in Windows Sound settings.
3. Reopen flyout; then re-enable and check again.
reproduce.expected_result: Disabled endpoint has no active control; enabled endpoint returns.
